content_units: You bring in   CAD 4,600   and currently spend   CAD 4,380  , leaving about   CAD 220/month   before any extra goals.
To free up   CAD 350/month   without touching retirement savings, the cleanest path is to cut flexible categories first, not fixed essentials or debt.
Category   Current   Proposed   Monthly Cut   Why this goes first
Clothing   CAD 180   CAD 80     CAD 100     Easiest pause; often deferrable for 1-3 months
Dining out   CAD 310   CAD 230     CAD 80     High discretion; still leaves room for 1-2 meals out
Misc   CAD 210   CAD 140     CAD 70     Usually leaks through small untracked spending
Entertainment   CAD 160   CAD 110     CAD 50     Can trim without cutting all fun
Subscriptions   CAD 94   CAD 44     CAD 50     Fast win if you cancel/rotate services
Formula: `Free cash target = Current surplus + Monthly cuts = 220 + 350 = CAD 570`
Option 1:   Pause clothing spending     Buy only true replacements for 2-3 months     Frees CAD 100
Option 2:   Cap dining out weekly     Limit to about   CAD 55/week       Frees CAD 80
Option 3:   Tighten miscellaneous spending     Set a hard cash/app cap for impulse purchases     Frees CAD 70
Option 4:   Cancel or rotate subscriptions     Keep only 1-2 core services at a time     Frees CAD 50
I treated   retirement savings as off-limits   and left   rent, transit, utilities, student loan, pet care, phone, gym, groceries, and travel sinking fund   unchanged in the main plan.
I also kept the cuts focused on categories that are most adjustable without creating major lifestyle disruption.
